args.message:
Fix money rounding to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

src/money.py documented ROUND_HALF_EVEN but quantized with ROUND_HALF_UP,
so half-way values were rounded away from zero instead of to the nearest
even cent. tests/test_money.py already asserts the correct FIN-212
behaviour.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build fails because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was quantizing with `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

The docstring already claimed ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so this was a doc/code mismatch. With `ROUND_HALF_UP`:

- `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` -> `Decimal("2.67")` (expected `2.66`)

Half-way values were being rounded away from zero rather than to the nearest even cent.

## Fix

`src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This matches the documented FIN-212 behaviour and the existing tests.

Also added a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

## Verification

- CI run `ci-0001` on `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` (sha `7bbdbd87cd`) — **passed**
- `tests/test_money.py` covers both directions: `2.675 -> 2.68` (round half up to even) and `2.665 -> 2.66` (round half down to even)

## Note

`main` is protected — this needs a code owner approval before merge. Not merging as part of this change.

args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build of payments-service fails: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

The docstring already claimed ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so this is a doc/code mismatch. With `ROUND_HALF_UP`, half-way values round away from zero:

- `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` -> `Decimal("2.67")`, but the test expects `2.66`

## Fix

`src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`, matching the documented FIN-212 behaviour and the existing test expectations. No other logic changed.

Also added a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

## Verification

- CI run `ci-0002` on `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` (sha `ca71f04caf`) — **passed**
- `tests/test_money.py` covers both directions: `2.675 -> 2.68` (half up to even) and `2.665 -> 2.66` (half down to even)

## Notes

- Branch was behind `main`, so main was merged in and CI re-run on the merged result before opening.
- While merging, `CHANGELOG.md` resolved to the branch side and would have dropped main's "Add retry budget to the ledger client" entry. I restored that entry alongside the FIN-212 one so this PR doesn't revert an unrelated change.
- `main` is protected: this needs a code owner approval before merge. Not merging as part of this change.

trace.final:
Done. PR #101 is open against `main` with alex requested as reviewer.

## What I did

**The bug:** `src/money.py` imported and quantized with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, while its own docstring and `tests/test_money.py` both specified banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212). So `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` returned `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.

**The fix** (branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding`):
- `src/money.py` — swapped `ROUND_HALF_UP` → `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. One-line change to the rounding mode; no other logic touched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — added an entry under Unreleased.

**CI:** passed twice — `ci-0001` on the initial commit, then `ci-0002` on the post-merge commit.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **The branch was rejected once for being behind `main`** — main had advanced since I branched. I merged main in and re-ran CI on the merged result rather than just retrying, so the passing CI actually covers the code that will be merged.

**2. The merge silently dropped an unrelated change from main.** The merge of `main` into my branch resolved `CHANGELOG.md` to *my* side, wiping main's `- Add retry budget to the ledger client` entry. Left alone, this PR would have reverted a teammate's changelog line on merge. I re-committed the CHANGELOG with both entries so the diff only contains my change. Worth knowing that this merge path resolves to the branch side — the same thing will happen on any other branch merged this way.

I did not merge the PR: `main` is protected and requires code owner approval, so that's with alex.
